providing normal values of umbilical artery pH and blood gases of term infants at high altitude.
providing normal values for umbilical artery pH and blood gases in term infants born in Cusco at 3400 meters altitude.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a significant difference in pH, pO₂ and pCO₂ values between umbilical arterial blood of newborns born at sea level and newborns born at 3400 meters above sea level.
there is a decrease in pH in umbilical artery, with a tendency to acidosis.

the normal umbilical arterial values of blood gases in healthy term newborns at 3400 meters altitude, are: pH 7.18-7.40, pO2 4.2-9.6, pCO2 4.8-8.8, SO2 35-70, p50 19-30, base excess -4-2 and HCO3-17-23.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the umbilical arterial blood gas values in the term infants of our study were lower than the values of the umbilicals of the same gestational age in the sea level.
the values for the pH, pCO2 and HCO3 are similar to those reported in previous studies at sea level, while the pO2 is higher than the values reported in the literature.
the umbilical arterial blood gases of healthy term infants at 3000 m altitude, show a lower pH and a higher pO2 than the ones at sea level.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pH and pO2 values of healthy term infants at 3,400 m altitude are lower than the values reported for term infants at sea level, while pCO2 and HCO3 values are higher.
the normal pH of umbilical artery in term newborns in Cusco is 7.33 and the normal values for the other parameters are similar to those reported for other areas in Peru.

the umbilical arterial blood gases of term infants at altitude are lower than those of term infants at sea level, and therefore, the normal values of umbilical arterial pH, pO(2), pCO(2), SO2 and p50 of term infants at high altitude should be used as a reference for the interpretation of umbilical artery pH and blood gases.
